title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Becomes Sole Longest-Leading Non-Holiday Hot 100 Hit With 20th Week at No. 1
summary: It becomes just the second song overall to reign for 20 or more weeks.
contentText:
Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” achieves a landmark 20th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — claiming the sole longest run ever atop the chart for a non-holiday song. The smash first led in February, has already set multiple chart records and is just the second title in the Hot 100’s 68-year history to lead for at least 20 weeks.

Here’s an updated look at the longest-leading hits, ranked by most weeks at No. 1 ever on the Hot 100:

- 22 weeks, “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” Mariah Carey, 2019-26

- 20, “Choosin’ Texas,” Ella Langley, 2026

- 19, “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” Shaboozey, 2024

- 19, “Old Town Road,” Lil Nas X feat. Billy Ray Cyrus, 2019

- 16, “Last Night,” Morgan Wallen, 2023

- 16, “Despacito,” Luis Fonsi & Daddy Yankee feat. Justin Bieber, 2017

- 16, “One Sweet Day,” Mariah Carey & Boyz II Men, 1995-96

The only song in the way of the run of “Choosin’ Texas” historically, Mariah Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas Is You” has ruled the Hot 100 each Yuletide season since the 1994 carol was first No. 1 in 2019, and could add to its total in the holidays ahead.

“We loved the song when we wrote it, but none of us thought that it would be the song to do everything it’s doing,” Langley told Billboard earlier this year of “Choosin’ Texas,” which she cowrote with Luke Dick, Miranda Lambert and Joybeth Taylor. “It keeps giving us a reason to celebrate new ­milestones.”

The Hot 100 blends all-genre U.S. streaming (official audio and official video), radio airplay and sales data, the lattermost metric reflecting purchases of physical singles and digital tracks from full-service digital music retailers; digital singles sales from direct-to-consumer (D2C) sites are excluded from chart calculations.
